steps.text: In the warm gold of late afternoon, three friends were playing in the berry dell.
Clover bounced. Bramble rolled. And Ruby the robin sang the very last song of the day.
Pop! went a berry, straight into Bramble's mouth.
But slowly, slowly, the shadows began to stretch — long and blue across the grass.
'Tonight,' said Clover, 'the fireflies dance in the deep woods. Come with us, Ruby! Come and see!'
Ruby's feathers went tight. The deep woods meant the dark.
And the dark was the one thing Ruby did not like.
They gathered at the old round stump, where forest plans have always been made.
'I do want to see the fireflies,' Ruby whispered. 'But the dark makes my wings feel small.'
Bramble shuffled close beside her.
'When I feel scared,' he said, 'I curl up round, take a big slow breath, and count. One. Two. Three.'
Ruby tried it. A big slow breath.
One. Two. Three.
It helped. A little.
But the sun slid lower, and lower still.

steps.text: The clearing was wide and golden, the last of the sunlight pooling in the grass.
'When I feel scared,' said Clover, 'I hop as LOUD as I can — so the dark knows a very brave rabbit is coming!'
Boing! Boing! BOING!
Ruby laughed until her tail feathers shook.
And then, at the far edge of the clearing, they saw it.
The fern tunnel. Deep, and green, and dim.

steps.text: The ferns arched over the path like a long green doorway, and at its far end the very last light of day was waiting.
Ruby stopped. Everything went very, very quiet.
Then — a breath. A big slow breath.
One. Two. Three.
Clover pressed close on one side. Bramble pressed close on the other.
And step by step, wing by wing, the three friends walked into the dim — together.
And then the dim began… to glow.
Soft blue mushrooms lit the path like rows of tiny lanterns. The evening woods were not black at all. They were silver, and blue, and gently, gently shining.
'Good evening, little ones,' said Owl, from her mossy doorway. 'Ruby — you look surprised. Did no one ever tell you?'
'The dark is just the day, resting. Look how softly it glows.'
Ruby looked. And looked.
And her wings did not feel small anymore.
At the fork in the night path, the show was just beginning.
Fireflies! One, then ten, then a hundred tiny lights, swirling like slow warm snow.
And there was Ruby, dancing in the middle of them all — the little bird who walked through the dark, and found it full of light.
When the dancing was done, the friends settled in the moonlit clearing, warm and close and heavy-eyed.
Bramble curled up round — no counting needed tonight.
Clover's long ears folded down, soft as petals.
And Ruby tucked her head beneath her wing, right in the middle of her friends.
Only Owl stayed awake, round-eyed and glad, keeping watch the way owls do.
The moon held still. The fireflies blinked — slow, and slower.
And the dark held them all. Soft, and kind, and quiet as a nest.
Goodnight, Ruby. Goodnight, little friends.
Goodnight.
